summary: Five findings: an unconditional false cΓ_v(I) characterization, missed preservation under ordinary completion, a summary confusing numerical-type Picard with metric-graph Jacobian, integral/generic period-space conflation in overlap notes, and a wrong Faltings-metric overlap. All 243 targets, 291 distinct cited declarations and 108 overlap entries checked; no target-library or layer-verdict changes proposed.
checked: Accepted AUDIT-39 at explorer a82b26b733748a9ebb58d0fac653c02a7c198d66, with REV-AUDIT-39: 36 layers and all 243 target contracts; independence from author and reviewer.

All 382 citation occurrences, 291 distinct declarations in 157 source files, read at Mathlib 082e2d37e8b0463410cdb532e111cd43d5a66174 and Tau Ceti f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369, including enclosing variable assumptions and construction bodies where needed. File/line/name resolution checked for every distinct declaration.

Every target labelled absent searched by concept and alternate terminology in declarations.tsv and both pinned source trees; nearby algebraic, scheme, topological and analytic results distinguished from the target carriers.

All 108 duplicate entries checked against both live atlas stage contracts and dependencies; supplier/consumer interfaces, absolute/relative specialization and parent/substage aggregates distinguished from duplicate ownership under PROTOCOL section 15.

All four focal roadmap documents, the three integrated decomposition node/coverage inventories and relevant input boundaries; data/library-coverage.json inspected (generated 2026-09-21, none of these 36 rows present). The accepted audit itself is the reviewed target, not an assumed coverage row.

107 pinned Huber/AdicSpace source files scanned with nested comments and strings removed: no direct sorry, admit or axiom tokens. This is a source check, not compilation or a transitive proof-dependency certification.

findings.where: research/blueprint/audit/AUDIT-39.result.json; AdicSpaces Layer 1, target 4 (zero-based), note on cΓ_v(I)
findings.claim: The note unconditionally characterizes cΓ_v(I) as the greatest convex subgroup for which I is cofinal. This is false in the branch where the ideal meets the characteristic subgroup. The cited greatest-subgroup theorem expressly assumes the opposite branch.
findings.evidence: Valuation.characteristicSubgroupOfIdeal, TauCeti/RingTheory/Valuation/CofinalIdeal/Greatest.lean:479, Tau Ceti f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369 defines an if: when IdealMeetsCharacteristicSubgroup v I, return characteristicSubgroup v; otherwise choose the greatest subgroup. The theorem isGreatestIdealCofinal_characteristicSubgroupOfIdeal at line 495 requires (h : ¬ IdealMeetsCharacteristicSubgroup v I). IdealCofinalFor at line 103 means every element of I is cofinal. Counterexample: I = ⊤ is finitely generated, its value set contains 1 in the characteristic subgroup, so the first branch applies. But 1 belongs to I and Valuation.not_cofinalValueFor_one (CofinalIdeal/Basic.lean:251) says its value is not cofinal for ANY subgroup. Thus the family in the unconditional greatest characterization is empty. Wedhorn, Adic Spaces, arXiv:1910.05934v1, Definition 7.3, printed p.56, has exactly this case split.
findings.fix: Replace the note with both branches of Definition 7.3 and attach the non-meeting hypothesis to the greatest characterization. Add characteristicSubgroupOfIdeal_of_meets (Greatest.lean:485) for the first branch. Keep the target library tauceti and Layer 1 verdict built: the correct definition and both branch statements are present. Include I = ⊤ as a regression check against an unconditional characterization.

findings.where: research/blueprint/audit/AUDIT-39.result.json; AdicSpaces summary and Layer 4 target 7, ordinary-completion clause
findings.claim: The audit lists preservation of strong noetherianness under separated completion as missing, overlooking a zero-variable specialization and bicontinuous transport already supplied by the pinned library. There need not be a separately named completion instance for this mathematical clause to follow.
findings.evidence: TauCeti.Huber.IsStronglyNoetherian.restrictedMvPowerSeriesCompletion, TauCeti/RingTheory/Huber/StronglyNoetherian.lean:161, Tau Ceti f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369 gives IsStronglyNoetherian (restrictedMvPowerSeriesCompletion k A) for every natural k under IsHuberRing A and IsStronglyNoetherian A. At k = 0, restrictedMvPowerSeriesCompletionFinZeroEquiv (WeightedRestrictedSeries/Completion.lean:286) identifies that ring with UniformSpace.Completion A for the canonical right additive uniformity. Continuity in both directions is proved at lines 329 and 339. isStronglyNoetherian_congr (StronglyNoetherian.lean:229) transports the predicate along that bicontinuous ring equivalence. A Tate base is Huber, so the audit target has the required hypotheses. This is stronger than the separately named isNoetherianRing_completion_of_isStronglyNoetherian, which only concludes ordinary noetherianness.
findings.fix: Credit the ordinary-completion clause as supplied by these existing statements, adding the instance at k = 0, zero-variable equivalence, both continuity lemmas and transport theorem as the evidence. Remove preservation itself from the summary of mathematical gaps. Keep target 7 partial and Layer 4 partly built: rational-localization/presheaf comparison under completion and the stably-sheafy/Tate-acyclicity conclusions remain missing. A convenience alias or instance may still be desirable; it is not a new mathematical proof obligation.

findings.where: research/blueprint/audit/AUDIT-39.result.json; TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic summary, phrase identifying Pic(T) with the combinatorial Jacobian TB.3 wants
findings.claim: The summary credits the discrete weighted numerical-type Picard group as the Jacobian required by TB.3. TB.3 asks for the Jacobian of a metric graph with piecewise integral-affine functions. The target-level note correctly distinguishes the objects; the summary contradicts it.
findings.evidence: TauCeti.NumericalType.Pic, TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Curves/StableReduction/Picard/Basic.lean:204, Tau Ceti f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369 is (T.Component → ℤ) modulo principalDivisors; principalDivisors at line 162 is the range of the weighted integer intersection matrix. finrank_pic (Picard/Rank.lean:186) proves rank one and finite_torsion (Picard/Torsion.lean:57) proves finiteness of each nonzero ℓ-torsion subgroup. These carriers contain no edge-length or real metric-graph divisor data. The current TB.3 contract says to construct divisors and piecewise integral-affine functions on metric graphs, their Laplacian and Jacobian, with a loop-graph acceptance test (content/campaign/TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic/README.md, TB.3). The audit TB.3 target 3 itself says that the real-torus Jacobian of a metric graph is absent.
findings.fix: Change the summary to call NumericalType.Pic a discrete weighted multidegree quotient useful as adjacent combinatorial infrastructure, with the cited rank-one and nonzero ℓ-torsion results. Explicitly retain the metric-graph Jacobian as missing. Leave TB.3 target 3 and the layer verdict unchanged. Do not identify all of Pic(T), its degree-zero/torsion part, a finite graph critical group, and a metric-graph Jacobian without comparison theorems.

findings.where: research/blueprint/audit/AUDIT-39.result.json; RF0:integral-Y duplicates with AdicSpaces Layer 6, FarguesFontaineDiamonds F0 and F1; reverse Layer 6 duplicate with RF0:integral-Y
findings.claim: The overlap notes conflate the integral period space retaining the characteristic-p fibre with the generic period domain. In particular, Layer 6 does not define exactly the integral 𝒴_S, and the F1 product formula with Spd ℚ_p is not the ℚ_p-coefficient specialization of the integral formula with Spd O_E.
findings.evidence: At explorer commit a82b26b733748a9ebb58d0fac653c02a7c198d66, RF0:integral-Y defines 𝒴_S = Spa(W_OE(R+)) \ V([varpi]), explicitly says its characteristic-p fibre is retained, and asks for 𝒴_S^diamond ≅ S × Spd(O_E). RF0:annuli separately removes V(pi) to obtain Y_S. AdicSpaces Layer 6.1 instead defines its differently named 𝒴 by D(p) ∩ D([ϖ]); F0 imports precisely that generic domain and warns that the open is the complement of the product zero locus. F1 proves Y_F^diamond ≅ S × Spd(ℚ_p) with p invertible. These statements are read in content/campaign/RelativeFarguesFontaine/README.md, content/tau-ceti/AdicSpaces/README.md and content/campaign/FarguesFontaineDiamonds/README.md and their atlas stage records. Setting E = ℚ_p changes O_E to ℤ_p, not to ℚ_p. Only restriction to D(p) gives the F1 generic formula.
findings.fix: Rewrite these four overlap notes as generic-open restriction/comparison interfaces: Layer 6 and F0 supply the fixed-field generic domain used after removing V(pi), and F1 supplies the product formula after base change from Spd ℤ_p to Spd ℚ_p. Direct the same-domain generic-annulus overlap to RF0:annuli, retaining RF0:integral-Y as the owner of the integral extension and special fibre. Do not remove that integral space or replace Spd(O_E) by Spd(E). Also qualify RF2:integral-divisors → F4 as only a generic degree-one comparison: F4 has no retained characteristic-p divisor fibre.

findings.claim: The note attributes overlapping nonarchimedean model metrics/local heights to R35.2. That specific stage constructs the Faltings metric on a Hodge determinant by integration at complex places. It does not supply TB.6's nonarchimedean analytic construction.
findings.evidence: At explorer commit a82b26b733748a9ebb58d0fac653c02a7c198d66, the R35.2 contract is titled The Hodge bundle and Faltings metric and says: "equip it with the metric defined by integration at complex places" (content/campaign/ArakelovGeometryAndAbelianHeights/README.md, R35.2; corresponding atlas stage). TB.6 constructs metrics from formal models and measures weighted by special-fibre intersection numbers, extending to semipositive metrics; its acceptance tests are the good-reduction Gauss-point mass and the uniform-length measure on a Tate circle (content/campaign/TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic/README.md, TB.6). No R35.2 theorem or object is identified that duplicates either construction.
findings.fix: Remove this R35.2 entry from the duplicate list, or explicitly classify it as a thematic archimedean comparison rather than a supplier/duplicate of TB.6. Preserve TB.6's nonarchimedean model-metric and measure obligations. Keep the separately evidenced TB.6 → GZ.2 overlap for nonarchimedean admissible pairings; do not transfer TB.6 to the complex Hodge-metric stage.
